summary: 100-foot wooden lookout built 1935 on Little Mountain, Mount Vernon, Skagit County, WA; removed or destroyed 1980; summit now in public Little Mountain Park.

facts.design: 100-foot wooden tower with a 7x7-foot cab and shake cabin; the register calls it the first lookout on the site
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1980: the register says removed, firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed.

access.note: Summit is inside Little Mountain Park, Mount Vernon; a 1.5-mile paved road leads to the top (Willhite)

visit.trail_note: Numerous hiking trails in the park; one climbs the mountain from the bottom of the park just after the entrance gate (Willhite)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the lookout was removed in 1980; firelookout.com and Willhite say it was destroyed in 1980. The year agrees, and the story reports both words.

The register names the Washington Division of Forestry/DNR as administrator. Willhite describes the summit as part of Mount Vernon's park. No source says who ran the 1935 lookout or who runs the park now, so the story reports both without choosing.

notes_for_editor: Three sources agree on the 1935 build, the 7x7 cab and the 1980 end; the 1942 AWS cabin is in all three. The register calls the 1935 tower 'the first lookout' but no source describes a later one, so none is written. Do not confuse this with the King County Little Mountain in the Cedar River watershed (a separate record; its Willhite page and weebly page were not used). No staffing or fire information was found. The 'Destroyed' versus 'removed' wording is unresolved; the story reports both. Park facts come from Willhite's Mount Vernon page. Height 30.5 m is the register's 100 feet converted.
